question: What is the difference between the System Global Area (SGA) and Program Global Area (PGA) in Oracle?
category: What is the difference between the System Global Area (SGA) and Program Global Area (PGA) in Oracle?

options.text: SGA is shared memory accessible to all Oracle background and server processes; PGA is private non-shared memory allocated per server process for sorting and session state.
A hard parse completely compiles the SQL, analyzes syntax, and computes an execution plan; a soft parse reuses an already compiled plan from the Library Cache using identical SQL text/bind keys.
It tracks block access frequency using a counter; blocks with high touch counts (>2) are protected from eviction when new blocks are read into the buffer.
LGWR synchronously writes the transaction's redo vectors from the Redo Log Buffer in SGA to the online redo log files on disk before acknowledging the commit.

explanation: SGA is shared memory accessible to all Oracle background and server processes; PGA is private non-shared memory allocated per server process for sorting and session state.
